content.title: About
content.content: Chocolate candy with nuts are sweet treats made from milk or dark chocolate combined with whole nuts such as hazelnuts, almonds, cashews, and others. The nuts add a crunchy texture and rich nutty flavor, while the chocolate provides sweetness and aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chocolate candies with nuts first appeared in Europe in the 19th century as a luxury confection.
The combination of chocolate and nuts creates a flavor contrast between sweet and bitter notes.
Nuts are often coated with a thin layer of chocolate, protecting them from oxidation.
In many countries these candies are a traditional gift for holidays and celebrations.
The cocoa content determines the amount of antioxidants present in the product.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Cocoa in chocolate contains flavonoids that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: Nuts provide monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that support heart health.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Nuts supply magnesium, iron, and zinc, essential for metabolic processes.

items.title: Mood‑enhancing
items.content: Chocolate stimulates the production of serotonin and endorphins, improving mood.

items.title: Adds plant protein
items.content: Nuts contribute plant‑based protein, helping to increase satiety.

items.title: Tree‑nut allergy
items.content: These candies can trigger severe allergic reactions in individuals sensitive to nuts.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive sugar may contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of dental caries.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Chocolate candy with nuts is energy‑dense, so it should be consumed in moderation.

items.title: Caffeine content
items.content: Dark chocolate contains caffeine, which can affect sleep if consumed in large amounts.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the candies as a standalone snack, add them to dessert platters, incorporate into baked goods, or use as a garnish for ice cream. In hot weather they can be kept refrigerated to keep the chocolate firm.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the candies in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For long‑term storage, keep them in the refrigerator, but allow them to reach room temperature before eating to avoid condensation.
